notes: cli/XM, cpi/XM: from the February 2015 edition the real-time database carries the euro-area aggregate as EA19 (Lithuania joined the euro area on 1 January 2015) instead of EA18; the aggregate is used as published.

cpi/CN: the August 2018 CPI edition stores a fixed-base index (y/y = 12-month ratio inside the vintage); the published y/y behind the one-full-month publication gate competes, and the published y/y (latest 2018-07) is used as the fresher series.

policy/JP: the BIS daily series is blank from 2013-04-04 to 2016-09-20; months without a BIS row carry the last BIS level as a proxy. From 2016-02-16 the rate applied to Policy-Rate Balances, -0.10% (announced 2016-01-29; source below the policy decisions), fills the blank days; the BIS series resumes at the same level on 2016-09-21.
policy/IN: BIS monthly differs from the daily month-end in 2007-03; monthly rows retained.

policy/TR: the one-week repo rate became the policy rate on 2010-05-20 (the BIS series switches from the overnight borrowing rate, 6.50% → 7.00%). The switch is not a rate change (CBRT Monetary Policy Committee decision No. 2010-16, 18 May 2010: overnight rates kept unchanged; as a 'technical rate adjustment', 'the one week repo rate, which becomes the new policy rate, is set at 7 percent—50 basis points above the overnight borrowing rates'): earlier history is spliced by +0.50pp so that policy changes are measured on the new instrument.

policy/ID: the BI 7-Day (Reverse) Repo Rate became the policy rate on 2016-08-19 (the BIS series switches from the BI Rate, 6.50% → 5.25%). The switch is not a rate change (Bank Indonesia press release No. 18/67/DKom, 19 Aug 2016: the Board of Governors (18–19 Aug 2016) held the BI 7-day Reverse Repo Rate at 5.25% and, as announced on 15 Apr 2016, 'terhitung mulai hari ini Bank Indonesia menggunakan BI 7-day RR Rate sebagai suku bunga kebijakan menggantikan BI Rate' (from today the BI 7-day RR Rate replaces the BI Rate as the policy rate); the BI Rate had stood at 6.50%): earlier history is spliced by -1.25pp so that policy changes are measured on the new instrument.

Ministry of Finance of China, International Economic and Financial Cooperation Center (in Chinese), 'OECD国家经济增势放缓', 12 Sep 2018: OECD-area CLI 99.7 in July, −0.11% on the month; China 99.9, +0.32%; India 101.6, +0.23%

policy_context.text: the CBRT lowered banks' borrowing limits at its Interbank Money Market to TL 22 billion from 11 Jan 2017 (announced 10 Jan) and to TL 11 billion from 16 Jan 2017, said funding through Borsa Istanbul repo markets 'may be limited' on days deemed necessary, and that banks could meet their remaining liquidity needs 'without limits at late liquidity window funding rate at the end of the day'; the one-week repo rate (the BIS series) stays at 8%, so it understates the CBRT's marginal funding cost from then on
policy_context.label: CBRT press release, 13 Jan 2017

policy_context.text: the MPC raised the marginal funding (overnight lending) rate from 8.5% to 9.25% and the late liquidity window lending rate from 10% to 11%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8%
policy_context.label: CBRT MPC decision, 24 Jan 2017

policy_context.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 11% to 11.75%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending rate at 9.25%
policy_context.label: CBRT MPC decision, 16 Mar 2017

policy_context.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 11.75% to 12.25%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending rate at 9.25%
policy_context.label: CBRT MPC decision, 26 Apr 2017

policy_context.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 12.25% to 12.75%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending rate at 9.25%
policy_context.label: CBRT MPC decision, 14 Dec 2017

policy_context.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 12.75% to 13.5%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending (marginal funding) rate at 9.25%
policy_context.label: CBRT MPC decision, 25 Apr 2018

policy_context.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 13.5% to 16.5% ('a strong monetary tightening'), keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending rate at 9.25%
policy_context.label: CBRT MPC decision, 23 May 2018

policy_context.text: the CBRT completed the simplification of its operational framework: from 1 Jun 2018 'one-week repo rate will be the policy rate of the Central Bank. This rate will be equal to the current funding rate (16.50%)', with the overnight borrowing and lending rates 150 basis points below/above it. The BIS series' move from 8% to 16.5% on 1 Jun 2018 therefore ends the late-liquidity-window funding regime (the marginal funding rate was already 16.5% from 23 May); it is not a further tightening on that day
policy_context.label: CBRT press release on the operational framework, 28 May 2018
